title: 6. Conclusion to Part I: A Strategy of Correlative Thinking
content:
On the great silk of history, the AI revolution is like a new thread, glittering with hope while also carrying the threat of unraveling existing patterns. To weave this thread harmoniously, humanity must remember the skill of the seasoned weaver—one who sees the whole design, understands the color and role of each thread, and has the patience and creativity to adjust when the pattern goes awry. In other words, we must take correlative thinking—relational, holistic thought—as our basic strategy.

### 6.1. The Organic Consilience of the Four Modes of Thought

The four modes of correlative thinking are not tools used separately but an engine that turns together. If multidimensionality makes us see reality from many angles, circulation makes us read the flow of time within those many angles; empathy makes us connect the hearts of people within that flow; and convergence combines all of it into new value. If any one is missing, the rest cannot function fully. Without seeing relationships multidimensionally, the depth of empathy too becomes shallow; without knowing the rhythm of circulation, one misses the timing of convergence.

Let us draw an analogy with a school project. Examining a topic from multiple perspectives when first choosing it is multidimensionality; the process of gathering, discarding, and reorganizing material is circulation; harmonizing and encouraging the opinions of group members is empathy; and making each one's output into a single completed presentation is convergence. Training these four in the AI era cultivates individual competitiveness, but, further, it is also the work of cultivating the civilizational capacity to convert conflict into *hwajaeng*.

The four-stage methodology presented in this work—multidimensionality (立體, Mimesis), circulation (循環, Mythos), empathy (共感, Logos), and convergence (融合, Theos)—constitutes, on the basis of correlative thinking, a coherent strategy that contributes to human adaptation and flourishing in the AI era. Each stage is interconnected and creates synergy: "multidimensional" understanding influences how we recognize "circular" patterns, and "empathy" becomes the essential condition for meaningful "convergence." This multidimensional approach lays the foundation by which the human can complement AI's analytic capacity, respond flexibly amid unpredictable change, and lead technology to accord with human-centered values. Daoist mimesis offers, through the principle of complementarity, the harmonious coexistence of AI and the human; Buddhist mythos, through the thought of dependent arising and emptiness, the wisdom of relational becoming; Confucian Logos, on the basis of benevolence (仁), a new relational ethics; and convergence, as the fourth mode of thought, embraces all of these and presents the path of new value-creation.

### 6.2. Toward a New Renaissance

In an AI-led world, the human correlative capacities—empathy, holistic understanding, ethical judgment, meaning-creation, and creative synthesis—are distinctively human strengths whose value rises all the more as AI handles routine analytic tasks. The AI era paradoxically demands of us "to cherish what makes the human human—that is, holistic intelligence—and to organize society accordingly." This is the path of opening a new horizon of the AI era through the deepening and manifestation of human distinctiveness, rather than competition with machines. AI is a powerful tool, but it cannot be an end in itself. The human must use AI as a means for realizing the ultimate purposes of human dignity and happiness and the prosperity of the community. This is to guard against techno-omnipotence, to restore human-centered value, and to orient toward a new renaissance that human and AI will make together.

### 6.3. Educational and Social Practice

Correlative thinking is not a difficult, complex Eastern philosophy but a concrete habit of thought that can be practiced in reality. The best way to cultivate correlative thinking in the educational field is the training of asking "why" and "how" together. Not merely finding the correct answer, but thinking together about why it is a problem, how it looks from another viewpoint, and whom the solution affects and how—this habit is the starting point of correlative thinking.

At the level of social practice, it is important to make spaces for "slow conversation." The AI era demands fast information and instant reaction, but correlative thinking and *hwajaeng* grow in the "slow conversation" that takes ample time to understand one another. Discussion gatherings in local communities, philosophy classes in schools, ethics-debate sessions in companies, the deliberative processes of government—when such institutional spaces of "slow conversation" remain alive even in the AI era, the practice of *hwajaeng* becomes possible.

AI companies and platforms, too, can take part in the practice of correlative thinking. Including users of diverse cultures, ages, and income classes when designing AI systems; regularly reviewing and disclosing algorithmic bias; providing content that educates users to use AI critically—all of these are the corporate-level practice of correlative thinking. The company that invests in the design of relationships with the human as much as in the speed of technological development will become the true leading company of the AI era.

The manifestation of such human attributes does not happen of itself. It requires conscious effort through education, policy-making, cultural development, and personal practice. The human must move beyond being a mere "problem-solver" to performing the role of "meaning-solver" within a complex world and technology. This will become the core driving force by which the human, without losing autonomy in the AI era, can develop technology in harmony with human values.

- **Educational innovation:** We must shift from memorization-centered education to an education that cultivates correlative-thinking capacities—critical thinking, creative problem-solving, empathy, and collaboration.
- **Redesign of social systems:** We must build an inclusive social system so that the benefits of technological development are shared across society as a whole and so that alienation by technology does not arise. A process is needed to establish AI ethical standards and to draw social consensus on the development and use of AI technology.
- **Cultural reflection and practice:** The individual must adapt to a changing age through ceaseless self-reflection and learning, and pursue a meaningful life in solidarity with others within the community. Effort is needed to apply correlative thinking to daily life and work.

The integration of Eastern wisdom and Western rationality, and of human capacity and AI tools, heralds the emergence of a new kind of human—technically adept yet possessed of deep wisdom—that is, the "wise cyborg" or "hybrid thinker." The Hallyu phenomenon can be seen as one example of such a successful strategy of synthesis, and "Hallyu as a new-human strategy of multidimensionality, circulation, and empathy" implies the possibility that cultural convergence presents.

Ultimately, what distinguishes and guides us in the hyperconnected world AI leads is the distinctively human capacity for holistic, interconnected reasoning, strengthened by bodily presence and intuition. Just as yin-yang taught that manifest opposites can form a larger whole, human intuition and artificial intelligence too, if approached wisely, can form a partnership greater than the sum of the parts. As the five phases remind us that balance and periodic renewal are the key to longevity, we must maintain a balance between technological advance and ethical, emotional, and cultural renewal. The stories and contingencies of life remind us that we are not the objects of algorithms but the subjects of destiny. If we remember that we are the ultimate connectors, we need not fear the hyperconnected future.

"The silk of civilization will surely take on a new pattern, but it will still be woven by human hands, according to a wisdom born of long-cherished hypothesis and imagination—and this will be a true triumph of hypothesis and imagination, made together by hypothesis and imagination." By thinking within the whole and within relationships, feeling deeply, creating boldly, and acting according to conscience, the human will be able, in the AI era, not merely to survive but to bloom within it.
